review.assumption: Hyperposition higher-order semantic identity requires a physically native n-ary runtime primitive.
review.shared_ancestry: Current Hyperposition and ClayCode designs share Clay project ancestry.
independent_evidence: Peixoto, Peel, Gross, De Domenico 2026 arXiv:2602.16937: graph-based models can represent multivariate/higher-order interactions; graph representation is not inherently limited to independent pairwise interactions.
Current project faceted-backend executable hidden-factor differential, treated as same-project discriminating evidence rather than independent replication.
review.decision: Preserve n-ary semantic identity and role bindings, but treat physical NATIVE_NARY as one backend option. Pairwise/factorized lowering is admissible only with semantic equivalence/projection receipts and cost/recovery comparison.

review.assumption: A single semantic/state generation fence is sufficient for rewrite/cache validity even when active, coordination or physical topology changes independently.
review.shared_ancestry: The four-topology law and HyperMath V1.1 are same-project artifacts; agreement cannot support the claim.
independent_evidence: Anderson et al. 2021 arXiv:2105.06712: self-adjusting computation tracks control/data dependencies and propagates changes through affected dependencies.
Budiu et al. arXiv:2203.16684 / PVLDB: DBSP derives incremental computations for rich query languages.

Local 100,000-case topology-scope falsifier: current V1.1-like key produced 33,368 unsafe reuses under intentionally same-generation non-semantic topology mutations; scoped key produced 0 in the declared-dependency model.
review.decision: Add compiler-visible TopologyReadEffect/TopologyScopeCertificate as an additive candidate; target promotion requires real Frank same-epoch topology mutation evidence and comparison against a simpler single topology-generation counter.

review.assumption: Proof/law metadata alone is sufficient to make HyperMath rewrites safe.
review.shared_ancestry: HyperMath RewriteWitness and ClayCode Rewrite structures are co-designed inside the same project.
independent_evidence: Egglog 2023 arXiv:2304.04332 supports efficient incremental execution plus equality-saturation/rewriting as a mechanism class, but does not establish Clay-specific safety.
Local negative test rejects a program whose observed ACTIVE topology read is absent from its declared exact scope.
review.decision: Rewrite law status must be combined with complete/conservative material-read closure and exact topology dependency scope. TESTED_BOUNDED remains bounded evidence, not universal proof.

review.assumption: The frozen V18 grammar must be changed to encode topology-read effects.
review.shared_ancestry: Hyperposition requests and ClayCode language design are same-project feedback.
independent_evidence: Current accepted-target ClayCode diagnostic localizes active work to frontend dispatch/TypedIR/type-effect issues and explicitly keeps V18 frozen.
The topology-scope checker demonstrates the candidate as TypedIR/type-effect metadata without any source grammar change.
review.decision: Do not reopen V18. Implement topology read effects after frontend parsing, in TypedIR/type-effect/compiler metadata, until an executable source-level counterexample proves syntax is necessary.

next_independent_discriminator: Accepted-target current frontend -> TypedIR -> WP04 compiler path plus real Frank topology mutation traces; compare scoped certificates against one coarse topology generation and existing V1.1 fence.
